question: If a suspect makes an utterance during an interview in Santa Cruz, what is the required police procedure before continuing?

[1] Act: TTPS Standing Orders | Chapter: Police Procedure | Section: Interview and Utterance Handling | URL: https://example.tt/ttps-standing-orders/interview-procedure
# TTPS Standing Orders - Interview Procedure
Act: TTPS Standing Orders
Chapter: Police Procedure
Section: Interview and Utterance Handling
URL: https://example.tt/ttps-standing-orders/interview-procedure

When a suspect makes an utterance during a police interview, officers must pause substantive questioning
and transition to a Statement under Caution process before continuing with further interview questions.

The suspect should be informed of the caution, and the statement should be recorded in accordance with
standing orders, preserving the suspect's exact words and context.

Where required by procedure, the statement and process must be authenticated by a Justice of the Peace
or other authorized officer before interview continuation.

[2] Act: TTPS Standing Orders | Chapter: Operational Orders | Section: Interview Procedure 5.3 | URL: https://example.org/ttps-standing-orders/interview-procedure
# TTPS Standing Orders - Recording and Authentication of Statements
Act: TTPS Standing Orders
Chapter: Operational Orders
Section: Interview Procedure 5.3
URL: https://example.org/ttps-standing-orders/interview-procedure

When a person under interview makes an incriminating utterance, interviewing officers must pause the interview process and transition to a formal Statement under Caution procedure.

The statement should be read back to the suspect, and where the procedure requires authentication, the suspect's statement is to be authenticated before a Justice of the Peace.

No further substantive questioning should continue until the required caution and authentication steps are completed and recorded.

[3] Act: Firearms Act | Chapter: 16:01 | Section: 4 | URL: https://www.legalaffairs.gov.tt/
# Firearms Act - Handling Utterances During Interview
Act: Firearms Act
Chapter: 16:01
Section: 4
URL: https://www.legalaffairs.gov.tt/

When a suspect makes an utterance during an interview, officers must avoid obtaining informal admissions outside the required legal safeguards.

Any substantive statement that may be relied upon should be reduced into a Statement under Caution process according to TTPS procedure and evidential rules.

Further questioning should proceed only after procedural safeguards are applied and recorded in the case documentation.
